title: Provider webhooks signed, chatbot widget on a public mount keyed by widget key
goal: Accept provider callbacks only when they are genuinely from the provider, and make the website chat widget work without a staff login.
why: Every route in routes/voip-callbacks.ts is public and unsigned although its header says signature-validated; /webhooks/twilio/status and /webhooks/sendgrid/events (routes/webhooks.ts) are unsigned; chatbot /webhook/:channel, /whatsapp/incoming and widget routes are mounted after authMiddleware and requireFeature (index.ts ~216, ~283), so the public widget gets 401.
steps: middleware/provider-signature.ts: verifyTwilio(req, url, params, authToken) (HMAC-SHA1 of URL + sorted params, base64, X-Twilio-Signature, constant-time compare) (Plivo callbacks: owner decision 2026-10-14, do not build Plivo-specific verification; a tenant whose provider is plivo is rejected at the signature step unless plivo-voice.ts validateWebhookSignature already works, and no test covers it), verifySendgrid (Signed Event Webhook: ECDSA P-256 over timestamp + raw body with X-Twilio-Email-Event-Webhook-Signature/Timestamp and the public key in SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY, WebCrypto importKey spki). Reuse the provider classes' validateWebhookSignature where they already implement it (services/voip-provider.ts).

voip-callbacks.ts: a middleware on every route resolves the tenant (callDb, R101) and verifies the signature with that tenant's provider credentials (decrypted by R108 when it lands; plaintext today) falling back to platform TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN; unsigned or invalid -> 403 and no DB write. The URL used for Twilio validation is the public URL: env.API_PUBLIC_URL + path (Workers see the real URL, but behind proxies use the configured one).

webhooks.ts: twilio/status uses verifyTwilio with the platform token; sendgrid/events uses verifySendgrid; when the key/secret env var is unset: reject in production, allow with a warning when isTestMode (R106 helper; if R106 has not merged yet use env.TEST_MODE === "true" && env.ENVIRONMENT !== "production").

Chatbot public mount: routes/public-chatbot.ts mounted before authMiddleware at /api/v1/public/chatbot: GET /:widgetKey/widget.js, GET /:widgetKey/config, POST /:widgetKey/messages. widgetKey resolves to a tenant through master tenant_channel_addresses (channel 'widget', address = widget key; add rows when an agency enables the widget: find where chatbot settings generate a widget key, else generate one in GET /chatbot/config and upsert the address). Plan feature ai_chatbot checked inside (requireFeature logic called as a function with the resolved tenantId). Limits per READINESS-PLAN 4.4 (30 messages / 10 min / IP / widget, 2 KB message, origin allow-list from chatbot settings, unknown key -> 404). Move the handler bodies from chatbot.ts into shared functions so the staff routes and the public routes call the same code.

WhatsApp chatbot incoming moves to /api/v1/webhooks/chatbot/whatsapp (signed, Twilio) and resolves the tenant from the To number via tenant_channel_addresses; remove the authenticated /chatbot/whatsapp/incoming and /chatbot/webhook/:channel mounts (keep the staff config/conversation routes behind auth).
Update existing voip-callbacks.test.ts and delivery-callbacks.test.ts helpers to sign requests with the test auth token (add a signTwilio helper in the test file).
tests: backend/test/webhook-signatures.test.ts: valid Twilio signature -> 200 and row updated; missing or wrong signature -> 403 and nothing written; SendGrid ECDSA valid (generate a key pair in the test with crypto.subtle.generateKey and pass the public key as env) / invalid.

backend/test/public-chatbot.test.ts: widget.js served without auth for a known key, 404 for unknown; POST message creates a chatbot conversation in the right tenant DB (multi mode); 31st message in 10 minutes from one IP -> 429; disallowed Origin -> 403; tenant without ai_chatbot -> 403 with upgrade flag.
acceptance: No public webhook route writes to a DB without a verified signature (outside test mode).
The widget works without a login (test).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
cd desktop && E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3110 E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8797/api/v1 npx playwright test e2e/chatbot.spec.ts e2e/webhooks-integrations.spec.ts e2e/calls.spec.ts
goLiveVerify: Twilio (or the ADR-001 addendum provider) signatures against real callbacks (proxy URL must match API_PUBLIC_URL); SendGrid signed event webhook enabled with its public key.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.
Provider callbacks are form-encoded; validate against the parsed form fields, not JSON.
chatbot.spec.ts is plan-gated and skipped on the pro e2e stack (FINAL-E2E.md); a skip is acceptable, a failure is not.
